newsitem.title: UK: Booker group sales up 36 pct in 1st 4 mths.
newsitem.headline: Booker group sales up 36 pct in 1st 4 mths.

text.p: Food distributor Booker Plc said on Wednesday that overall group sales, including those from Nurdin & Peacock, were up 36 percent in the first four months of the current year.
Chairman Jonathan Taylor told the annual meeting that UK cash and carry sales are ahead by five percent on a like-for-like basis in the same period.
About two thirds of the company's overall profits come from cash and carry.
"The group is on track to achieve all its main objectives, including our anticipated increase in earnings and debt reduction in 1997 and 1998," Taylor said in a statement.
He said the integration of the Nurdin & Peacock cash and carry business is proceeding on schedule.
"We are initially reviewing the future of cash and carry depots in 13 locations and as a result of that review we have recently announced the closure of the first five".

Taylor said it was normal for Booker's profits to be skewed to the second half. "This will be even more pronounced following the acquisition of Nurdin & Peacock, where sales and profitability, as in Booker Cash & Carry, are predominantly in the last part of the year and linked to Christmas, whereas the costs of acquisition are evenly distributed over the year".
